intent: Make the website deploy apply Caddyfile changes and survive a replaced dist/ directory, instead of reporting a healthy container that serves 404s.
scope: Non-goal: no change to the Gitea stack, the firewall step, the build, or the edge reload
changes: start_website now runs docker compose up -d --force-recreate; compose cannot detect a bind-mounted Caddyfile's contents changing, nor a bind mount left on an unlinked inode, so it reported 'Running' and applied neither
wait_for_website records the actual HTTP status instead of using curl -sf, so a failure distinguishes 'no response' from 'answered 404' -- different bugs that had one message
The 404 message names the two real causes: a stale /srv bind mount, or an empty dist/

verification.evidence: Container 'Up 6 hours', Caddy logs healthy, but docker exec ls /srv returned empty and curl 127.0.0.1:8088/ returned 404; dist/ had been replaced with a new inode (84695030) after container start

verification.command: rm -rf dist && pnpm build, then curl
verification.evidence: Reproduced deterministically: inode 84695030 -> 84695031, container /srv empty, curl -> 404

verification.command: source website_build.sh && start_website (patched), against that broken state
verification.evidence: Container Recreated; /srv lists assets blog cv.pdf index.html; / -> 200, /blog/hello-world -> 200 with title 'Hello, world — Krzysztof Rudnicki'

risks: Every deploy now restarts the static container, so there is a sub-second window where the loopback port refuses connections; the edge Caddy retries and the wait loop tolerates it
--force-recreate discards any state inside the container; this service is a read-only static file server and holds none
rollback: Drop --force-recreate and restore the curl -sf wait loop
After rollback, verify a Caddyfile edit actually takes effect by curling a prerendered blog post and checking its <title>, since that is what silently regresses
